Gideon's Trumpet: How One Man's Plea for Counsel Overturned a Precedent
A courtroom in Florida, USA. A man accused of breaking into a pool hall asked the judge for help. He said he had no money and asked to be provided with a lawyer.
The judge refused. The man replied, "The United States Supreme Court says I have the right to be provided with a lawyer."
The man's name was Clarence Earl Gideon. He was a defendant with no money and no legal training. Standing in his way were state law and a precedent that the federal Supreme Court had set itself.

The dispute that began in this courtroom where he was denied a lawyer would eventually reach the federal Supreme Court. And the Supreme Court would have to face the precedent it had set 21 years earlier once again.
